newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries static in quiet London trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries static in quiet London trade.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were largely unchanged on Friday from their overnight falls in New York, as the absence of any data left prices rangebound and trading lifeless, traders said.
"I haven't done a customer trade all day," said a dealer at an American bank in London. "The market is unchanged from New York, and it's likely to stay that way as far as I can see."
The 30-year benchmark bond yielding 6.86 percent, was trading at 95-14 at 1127 GMT, from 95-13 in Tokyo and 95-15 at the New York close.
At the short end, five-year notes were unchanged from Tokyo at 99-17 and up from 99-00 in New York, while two-year notes were 99-22 versus 99-21 in Tokyo and 99-22 in New York.
"We had some Japanese liquidation overnight, selling Treasuries at the long end of the market, but there's nothing going on in London," said a trader at another American bank.
With no data due out until next week, traders said the only event of the day would be the expiration of February options contracts in Chicago.
"The market's completely rangebound, and that's going to hold us right the way through next week," the trader said.
But the employment cost index for the fourth quarter of 1996, due on Tuesday and the fourth quarter GDP figure due on Friday are expected to spark some reaction in the market.
Traders said the previous day's auction of five-year notes had not been well absorbed by the market and had forced some players to liquidate long positions in New York.
"Distribution was not great," the trader said, "the market got buried."
March T-bond futures were at 110-21, down 7/32 in automated trade.
